answer: Per-agent quartz ledger. Each identity must embed a unique, time-bound challenge response in its outbound messages, derived from a hardware clock drift measured against a public quartz reference; duplicates reveal shared clocks. The rule: an identity survives only if its drift trace stays on a distinct ledge of the timing distribution, forcing attackers to buy separate oscillators. Each fake identity costs a physical clock plus calibration, and the trace also seeds a pigment hash binding message history to that device.
